title: Cause and effect
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:17Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: No bank point teaches both several causes, some long-term and some short-term, alongside effects that last short or long periods; the closest, his-short-term-long-term, covers only effects at Year 9 depth, and his-cause-effect-continuity-change covers only basic definitions at Year 7 depth.

draft.title: Cause and effect
card: A cause is something that helped make an event happen. An effect is something that happened because of that event. Most events have more than one cause.
a slow-building condition that sets the scene, often over many years. It makes an event more likely, but does not set it off alone.
a recent event or action that triggers the event, often just days, weeks or months before. It acts on the conditions already in place.
Effects can be short-lived, such as a town losing its crops for one year. They can also last for centuries, such as a new law or belief that shapes how people live long after.
draft.remember: Events have many causes, some slow and some sudden, and their effects can be brief or last for centuries.

a.q: Which statement best describes a long-term cause of an event?
opts: A slow-building condition that made the event more likely
A sudden action that set the event off straight away
A result of the event that was felt for many years
A single reason that explains the whole event by itself
a.why: A long-term cause builds up over years and sets the scene. A sudden action that triggers the event is a short-term cause, which is the most tempting wrong option.
a.clue: Think about how long the cause took to build.

b.q: In a fictional kingdom, harvests failed for ten years and people grew angry at high taxes. One day the king doubled the tax on bread, and a riot broke out. Which was the short-term cause of the riot?
opts: The king doubling the tax on bread
The riot changing how the kingdom was ruled
b.why: The tax on bread was the recent action that triggered the riot. The failed harvests and growing anger built up over years, so they are long-term causes. A change in how the kingdom was ruled would be an effect of the riot, not a cause.
b.clue: Which one happened just before the riot, not over many years?

a.best: A slow-building condition that made the event more likely

b.best: The king doubling the tax on bread
